newsitem.title: INDIA: India and Bangladesh to work to end water dispute.
newsitem.headline: India and Bangladesh to work to end water dispute.

text.p: India and Bangladesh agreed on Wednesday to try to hammer out an agreement to end a decades-old water-sharing dispute before the onset of the dry season in December, officials said.

Both countries renewed their pledge to find a solution to the issue at meetings between between visiting Bangladesh Water Resources Minister Abdur Razzak and Indian leaders including Prime Minister H. D. Deve Gowda and Foreign Minister I.K. Gujral.
Razzak met Indian Water Resources Minister Janeshwar Mishra on Tuesday and identified measures needed to forge a consensus on the issue.
The Ganges dispute has been a major irritant in relations between the two neighbours since India built its Farakka barrage near Bangladesh's northern border in 1974.
Dhaka says the barrage 18 km (11 miles) from Bangladesh's northern border obstructs the river flow and deprives the country of its fair share of water.

It says India diverts much of the water to meet its own requirements for irrigation and navigation during the dry season, while releasing excess water during the monsoon, causing extensive flooding in Bangladesh.

The Press Trust of India (PTI) quoted an Indian foreign ministry spokesman as saying both countries decided to make genuine efforts to finalise an agreement on the issue before the beginning of the dry season.
"The process to find a solution will continue," a Bangladesh official, who asked not to be identified, said.
He said no fresh dates were decided for the next round of discussions.
Razzak also met Jyoti Basu, chief minister of West Bengal state bordering Bangladesh on Wednesday.
Bangladesh officials say more than 40 million people in north and north-western Bangladesh are seeing their land gradually turning into desert because of the Farakka barrage.
